name: HPV vaccine (human papillomavirus)
protects_against: HPV infections that can cause several cancers and genital warts

indications.reason: HPV vaccination is recommended for everyone through age 26 who hasn't completed the series.
For adults aged 27 to 45, HPV vaccination is a shared decision between you and a healthcare professional.

not_indicated_reason: HPV vaccination is recommended through age 26, and may be discussed from 27 to 45. It isn't part of the schedule after 45.

series.note: Adults usually need 3 doses. People who started before their 15th birthday may need only 2; a professional can confirm.

contraindications.text: A severe allergic reaction (such as anaphylaxis) after a previous dose, or to a vaccine ingredient.
Pregnancy. HPV vaccination is not recommended until after pregnancy. A pregnancy test isn't needed before vaccination.

precautions.text: A moderate or severe illness right now, with or without fever.

content.disease: HPV infections can cause cervical, vaginal and vulvar cancers in women, penile cancer in men, and anal and throat cancers in both men and women.
content.why: The vaccine prevents infection with the HPV types that cause most of these cancers. It works best before any exposure to HPV.
content.who: Everyone through age 26. Adults aged 27 to 45 may choose it after discussing it with a healthcare professional.
content.doses_text: Three doses for most adults: the second 1 to 2 months after the first, the third 6 months after the first.
content.catch_up: If you started the series earlier, you don't need to restart. The remaining doses can be given.
common_reactions: Soreness, redness or swelling where the shot was given
serious_reactions: People sometimes faint after medical procedures, including vaccination.
A severe allergic reaction is very rare.
